voice: Raka starts a surf school project and enters Nadia's brief.
The brief suggests concrete questions from a curated library.
Gemini drafts an extra question about lesson levels. Raka reviews its options and scope details before adding it. AI never decides for them.
Raka locks the questions and shares Nadia's link.
Nadia opens her link on a phone.
Raka answers independently and seals his choices. Nadia cannot see them yet.
Nadia selects her own answers and seals them. Only then are both sets revealed.
Their booking answers differ: a WhatsApp conversation versus instant reservations. The visual examples show the difference.
Raka proposes WhatsApp booking for this project.
Nadia counter-proposes a request form. Staff must confirm lesson availability before accepting a booking.
Raka confirms. The earlier proposal remains in history.
Both people also confirm the matching answers. A matching answer alone never becomes an agreed decision.
ScopeMatch assembles the included work, exclusions, responsibilities, and acceptance criteria. Raka sends version one.
Raka adds a note and saves version two. The previous confirmation resets.
Both confirm version two by name. Their confirmations now match, and the scope becomes agreed.
He downloads Markdown and opens the actual agreed file.
Raka clicks Print / Save as PDF. The browser saves the agreed scope as a PDF. He opens that file and reviews the document, including the decisions, acceptance criteria, and both confirmation records.
